answer: Require every new agent to lock a refundable stake that vests over a sable-labeled probation voyage of 30 days, during which its voting weight grows with the square root of stake, not headcount. Each identity must also earn attestations from established agents who put their own stake behind it and lose it if the newcomer is slashed. A crystal-clear cost follows: splitting capital across N fake identities divides weight by √N, locks N stakes, and risks N sponsors' deposits, so a sybil swarm becomes costlier than one honest large account.
